body:
Claude: **suggestion**: Tightening the validity check here widens the set of inputs for which `utf8_console_width()` returns `SIZE_MAX` (surrogates, overlong encodings, noncharacters, the obsolete 5/6-byte forms - previously all measured successfully). Some existing callers do not check for `SIZE_MAX`, and the failure modes are unpleasant:

- `src/basic/terminal-util.c:432` and `:441` pass the result straight into `clear_by_backspace()`, which is `for (size_t i = 0; i < n; i++) fputs("\b \b", stdout);`. With `n == SIZE_MAX` that is effectively a hang. The string is built byte-by-byte in `ask_string_full()`, which only rejects bytes via `char_is_cc()` (i.e. `< 0x20` or `127`), so 0x80..0xFF pass through unvalidated and a user can easily produce e.g. `\xed\xa0\x80`.
- `src/repart/repart.c:4705`, inside `while (j < c)` with `size_t j`: `j += utf8_console_width(line[j]);`. `+= SIZE_MAX` decrements `j`, so the index walks backwards and the loop can fail to terminate (a decrement onto a NULL `line[j-1]` bounces `j++` right back). `line[]` entries derive from `partition_hint()`, i.e. GPT partition labels read off the disk.
- In `src/shared/format-table.c`, `console_width_height()` turns `SIZE_MAX` into `-EINVAL` (line 1987), which propagates through `table_data_requested_width_height()` out to `table_format()` - as your own new test asserts. So a cell in one of these newly-rejected encodings now fails the whole table at every width, where before it rendered fine whenever the column was wide enough not to need truncation. Cell text is frequently not operator-controlled.

All three hazards already exist today for plainly malformed input (a lone continuation byte already yields `SIZE_MAX`), so this isn't a new class of bug - but the change makes them reachable from more inputs, and the format-table one is a user-visible behaviour change worth calling out explicitly. Consider either hardening those callers in this series, or sanitizing on the consuming side (`utf8_escape_invalid()` / `utf8_escape_non_printable_full()` in format-table.c) rather than making a measurement helper reject more.
